scope_note: This is the generation-6 corrective pass responding to the independent Codex rejection of PR #5620 (exact head 8f19ee4ea4587cc0ab2e11596221221125cd84be, frozen base 55cd327b9200648e5d42360907dedc17ddf6f5fc), which found 9 must-fix/should-fix defects on top of the generation-5 delivery. Each is fixed with real code changes: (1) tenant/supplied-ID authorization on aggregate resolution — POST /api/registry/strategy-specs' replay-return path now runs the returned view through _authorize_write before responding (a same-key/same-content replay previously skipped tenant scoping entirely); GET .../latest-approved and GET .../deployment-view now resolve against only the entries the caller's verified tenant (or admin/builtin) may see, via a new `visible` predicate parameter on RegistryService.resolve_latest_approved/resolve_deployment_view; the next-legal-version lookup in _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage is scoped the same way, so a cross-tenant strategy_id no longer perturbs another tenant's version sequence. (2) schema/route-contract enforcement — POST /api/registry/strategy-specs now runs the existing paper_strategy_spec.validate_strategy_spec JSON-schema validator on every inline strategy_spec before hashing/storing it (previously hashed an arbitrary dict with no schema check at all: strategy_spec={} returned 200); the generic POST /api/registry/entries route now schema-validates and checksum-verifies an embedded metadata.strategy_spec if the caller supplies one, while leaving the existing checksum-only reference-entry pattern (no embedded content) untouched. (3) version/base concurrency — RegistryStore.create/PostgresRegistryStore.create (the plain, non-register_if_absent create path used by register()) now accept and atomically enforce the same (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) unique_fields reservation register_if_absent already had, closing a race the prior generation left only guarded by a non-atomic application-layer pre-check; the next-legal-version computation is now tenant-scoped (see item 1). (4) immutable original receipts / caller CAS on creation — POST /api/registry/entries now accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header; RegistryService.register_with_idempotency + a new create_with_receipt on both storage backends (mirroring commit_metadata_cas's atomic reservation-then-commit pattern, sharing one Postgres transaction with the entry insert) makes a retried identical request return the originally-created entry instead of synthesizing a fresh random strategy identity every time. (5) outbox/recovery — not built in this pass; recorded honestly as a residual gap below rather than claimed done (see not_covered_in_this_delivery). (6) BFF identity/receipt truth — StrategyCommandAdapter._execute_update_params now verifies the caller-supplied registry_id actually belongs to the requested strategy_id (both on the PATCH response and any readback), failing closed with STRATEGY_ID_MISMATCH on a cross-aggregate write, and reports the entry's real semver `version` field in the receipt instead of mislabeling updated_at as version. (7) BFF replay and unconfirmed outcomes — a genuine idempotent replay (X-Idempotent-Replay: true) is now trusted directly from the PATCH response instead of being re-verified against an independent 'current' owner GET (which spuriously failed once a later, unrelated command had moved the row on); a readback failure immediately after a *confirmed* commit is now reported as ActionUnavailableError(READBACK_UNAVAILABLE, retryable=True, downstream_status=503) instead of the same flat non-retryable 422 used for a genuinely unsupported action — command_adapters/base.py's ActionUnavailableError gained retryable/downstream_status fields and command_executor.execute_command_with_status now propagates them instead of hardcoding 422/False. (8) explicit backend/readiness — services/registry/main.py now registers a `registry_owner` health dependency that performs a genuine short-lived Postgres connection probe (fresh connect + SELECT 1, never a cached pool) on every /readyz check, or explicitly reports degraded/backend=memory when the in-memory test double is selected, instead of registering no dependency at all (which previously made /readyz always report 200/ready=true/dependencies={} regardless of owner reachability). (9) contract/evidence accuracy — first_release_contract.json and this evidence file are updated to describe exactly what changed and what remains open in this pass, replacing the generation-5 claims the reviewer found stale (a claimed-never-a-separate-re-GET adapter description, and an evidence file that declared all findings fixed while recording unresolved gaps).

summary: service.py: _can_read split into _can_read_entry(ctx, entry)/_can_read(ctx, view); register_strategy_spec authorizes the replay-return view via _authorize_write before responding; _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage takes a required ctx and scopes its existing-versions lookup to entries visible to the caller; latest_approved/deployment_view routes pass a `visible=_can_read_entry(ctx, ...)` predicate into RegistryService; _strategy_spec_register_payload now runs validate_strategy_spec on every inline strategy_spec and rejects schema errors before hashing; _resolve_entry_or_draft_payload schema/checksum-validates an embedded metadata.strategy_spec on the generic route; register_entry accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header and routes through the new RegistryService.register_with_idempotency when present.

split_api.py: resolve_latest_approved/resolve_deployment_view gained an optional `visible` entry predicate (unscoped call sites are unaffected — they still delegate straight to the store's existing unscoped implementation); register() now passes unique_fields into store.create and maps RegistryUniqueViolationError to RegistryConflictError; new register_with_idempotency wraps store.create_with_receipt with the same validation register() applies.

storage.py / pg_store.py: new RegistryUniqueViolationError; RegistryStore.create/PostgresRegistryStore.create accept unique_fields and atomically reserve the composite identity (previously only create_if_absent did); new create_with_receipt on both backends implements the reservation-then-commit idempotent-creation pattern described in item 4 above, sharing one Postgres transaction with the entry insert on the durable backend.

main.py: added _registry_owner_dependency (a genuine Postgres connection probe, or an explicit memory-backend degraded report) and registered it as the `registry_owner` health dependency passed to register_fastapi_health_routes.
command_adapters/base.py: ActionUnavailableError gained retryable (default False) and downstream_status (default 422) fields.

command_adapters/strategy_adapter.py: _execute_update_params verifies the returned/readback entry's strategy_id matches the requested strategy_id (STRATEGY_ID_MISMATCH otherwise); a replay is trusted directly from the PATCH response with no second readback call; a readback failure after a confirmed commit raises with retryable=True, downstream_status=503; the receipt's version field now reports entry.version, not entry.updated_at.
command_executor.py: execute_command_with_status now reads downstream_status/retryable off the raised ActionUnavailableError instead of hardcoding 422/False.

test_registry_positives.py / test_service.py: added a schema-valid StrategySpec builder helper (_valid_spec) and updated every POST /api/registry/strategy-specs fixture in these two files to submit schema-complete payloads, since the dedicated route now actually enforces the schema (previously minimal {strategy_id, spec_version} payloads passed only because no validator ran); added regression tests for cross-tenant latest-approved leakage, the plain-create atomic unique_fields guard, and Idempotency-Key replay/non-replay behavior on POST /api/registry/entries; added a readiness-dependency unit test for main.py's memory-backend degraded report.

test_strategy_registry_owner_prerequisite.py: added a strategy_id field to existing mocked PATCH/readback entry fixtures (the new cross-aggregate check requires it); added regression tests for STRATEGY_ID_MISMATCH, replay-skips-second-readback, and readback-failure-after-confirmed-commit-is-retryable.

A full outbox/prepare-activate-reconcile crash-window proof (killing the server process between 'entry committed' and 'response sent', or between 'receipt reserved' and 'entry inserted' for the new create_with_receipt path) remains not built — this is finding 5 from the rejection and is the largest remaining architectural gap; create_with_receipt gives atomic reservation-then-commit correctness for the create path specifically (a crash mid-transaction rolls back the whole thing, including the reservation), but there is no standalone outbox event table, no prepare/activate/reconcile protocol, and no test that actually kills the process mid-transaction to prove it.

advance_artifact_state still has no caller-supplied Idempotency-Key/command-receipt of its own (only a server-side CAS base re-read each call); a retried advance under network loss is safe (CAS makes a duplicate a no-op or a clean 409) but does not return the original receipt the way update_metadata_cas/register_with_idempotency now do.

Real governance-review/promotion/runtime HTTP integration for submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive remains out of this task's owned scope (those owners are named in architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §4's consumer table).

The readiness dependency's Postgres connection probe is genuine (fresh connect + SELECT 1, not a cached pool) but no test in this pass kills a live database mid-run to observe the readiness transition to error status end-to-end; it is proven only for the memory-backend degraded case.
